what: Daily verbatim-echo baseline of GDELT's English-monitored news stream, re-implementing the nightly Consensus measurement (method v2) over the whole historical archive. One row per UTC day. Git is the archive: this file is computed once and committed, never read at runtime.

method.echo_index: share of titled articles sharing at least one >=3-domain 6-gram with another outlet
differences_from_nightly: the baseline day is a UTC calendar day; the nightly pool is a rolling 24 h window ending at the last completed quarter hour, so the two are comparable but not identical
the baseline classifies the day's widest phrase on ALL its domains; the nightly classifies on its display list of at most 40 mastheads (see the dated note in refresh.py)
HTML entities become token separators here (Python unescapes them first); both drop non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters, so titles tokenize the same in practice
translingual rows are excluded (TranslationInfo empty), matching the nightly's English-monitored raw files

window.starts_when_the_material_starts: 2019-09-22 is the first day the English GKG stream carries PAGE_TITLE — measured, not assumed: probed mid-June days from 2015 to 2026 return 0 title-bearing rows through 2019-06 and full coverage from 2019-10. The first day is itself partial (45,719 titled articles against ~190,000 the next day). A verbatim-title instrument therefore has seven years of history, not ten.

gaps.note: GDELT publishes no GKG partitions for these days; the gap is recorded, never interpolated.
gaps.thin_note: days far below the 132,633-article median are kept and disclosed, not dropped

source.name: GDELT GKG 2.1 via BigQuery (gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg_partitioned)
source.license_notice: GDELT requires citation and a link on any use or redistribution. This derived file is published with that notice rather than as bare CC0.

provenance.cost: 482.3 GB billed across 8 jobs = 44% of BigQuery's 1 TiB monthly free tier -> 0.00 EUR
provenance.compute_footprint: one-off batch: eight BigQuery jobs, no runtime dependency. Re-running the whole window costs the same scan again; the committed file is the artifact, not the query.
